proposed_fix.description: Verify whether productcatalogservice is hitting socket or connection limits on its pod or node, and if confirmed, relieve pressure with gated, reversible changes such as adding replicas or restarting a single pod.
steps: Inspect socket state on the productcatalogservice pods (e.g. ss -s, counts of ESTABLISHED/TIME_WAIT/CLOSE_WAIT) and compare with the baseline to see what drives the socket metric spike.
Check the node hosting the pods for conntrack usage versus its limit (nf_conntrack_count vs nf_conntrack_max) and for NIC receive errors; only pursue R1 or R4 if these are actually elevated.

Review client connection behavior from frontendservice, recommendationservice and checkoutservice (E3 callers): connection pooling, keep-alive and gRPC channel reuse, to detect connection churn or leaks.
If socket exhaustion is confirmed, with approval scale productcatalogservice replicas up by a small increment to spread connections.
If one pod shows abnormal socket counts, with approval restart that single pod and watch latency-50/90 and the socket metric.
If conntrack is confirmed near its limit, with approval raise nf_conntrack_max modestly on the affected node, recording the original value.
preconditions: Confirm the socket and latency anomaly is still ongoing, not already recovered.
Confirm cluster has capacity for extra replicas and that a restart of a single pod will not drop below minimum availability.
Confirm no deployment or rollout is in progress that could explain the change (check recent deploy history).
Get on-call engineer approval before any scale, restart, or sysctl change.
proposed_fix.rollback: Scale productcatalogservice back to the original replica count, restore the original nf_conntrack_max value if changed, and re-deploy the prior pod if a restart worsened behavior; all changes are small and individually revertible.
